title: Jacquard-woven silk bookmark
shortDescription: A woven silk bookmark made in the town in the 1890s, showing the Institute building in fine black and cream thread.

children.text: Woven on a Jacquard loom at one of the town’s silk mills, this bookmark was sold to raise funds for the Institute’s first reading room.
The picture is built from thousands of tiny warp threads, each lifted by a punched card. The weaver’s initials are stitched into the lower edge.

title: Silk throwster’s bobbin
shortDescription: A beech wood bobbin used to twist raw silk into thread, found in a mill workshop before it closed.

children.text: Throwsters twisted raw silk fibres into strong thread ready for weaving. This bobbin still carries a few strands of undyed silk.
It was given to the museum by the family of a former mill foreman.

title: Minute book of the Mechanics’ Library
shortDescription: The handwritten minutes of the committee that founded the town’s first lending library.

children.text: This leather-bound book records the early meetings of the Mechanics’ Library committee, including the first list of books bought for members.
Many of the founders were mill workers, who paid a penny a week to borrow from the shelves.

title: Silk and Stories: a guided gallery tour
description: Join one of our volunteer guides for a relaxed tour of the silk collection. You will see looms, pattern books and finished cloth, and hear stories from the people who worked in the mills. Suitable for all ages. Tea and coffee afterwards in the café.

seo.title: About the Institute
seo.description: A library, museum and art gallery sharing the story of our town and its silk heritage.

children.text: The Nicholson Institute is a library, museum and art gallery in the heart of the town. Since 1890 it has been a place to read, learn and enjoy art.
Our collections tell the story of local people and the silk industry that shaped the town.

content.heading: Free to visit
content.text: Entry to the library, museum and gallery is free. Open Tuesday to Saturday, 10am to 5pm.
